item.title: IC women’s track and field dominates in pole vault
item.description: The Ithaca College women’s pole vaulters have become a standout event group of the track and field team. Having athletes who have qualified for nationals and several who continue to place well at meets, the team creeps toward the tail end of its season with high expectations. The post IC women’s track and field dominates in pole vault appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Gymnastics’ record breaking event is not enough to stop a rival
item.description: Despite falling to the SUNY Cortland Red Dragons 192.800-191.350, Ithaca College gymnastics finished its last home meet of the 2026 season by making history, breaking the all-time IC gymnastics program team score in floor exercise, a 48.950, Feb. 11 in the Ben Light Gymnasium. The Bombers also posted their highest score of the season by 1.4 points. The post Gymnastics’ record breaking event is not enough to stop a rival appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Unknown Stage plants roots with February concert residency
item.description: Unknown Stage, a club unaffiliated with Ithaca College but made up of IC students that organize shows in Ithaca, is putting on a show every Friday night in the month of February. Though the organization hosts frequent shows each month, the February shows are all hosted at the Nocturnal Cafe, making this series of shows the first-ever Unknown Stage “Residency.” The post Unknown Stage plants roots with February concert residency appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Civil Rights photojournalist visits IC during annual MLK celebration
item.description: On Feb. 11, Ithaca College hosted its annual Martin Luther King Jr. keynote address as part of the campus wide MLK Celebration Week during Black History Month. The 2026 guest speaker was Cecil J. Williams, a South Carolinian Civil Rights leader, photojournalist, author and historian. The post Civil Rights photojournalist visits IC during annual MLK celebration appeared first on The Ithacan.

item.title: Students rethink sleep in spring semester
item.description: With the spring semester in full swing, students at Ithaca College are reconsidering their sleep schedules. Winter brings about a host of changes: new schedules, less sun and colder months keeping everyone inside. Sleep often changes as well. item.title: Fellowship of Christian Athletes combines love for faith and the field
item.description: In a small college of approximately 4,700 students, students create many ways for their peers to engage in a niche community. Every Tuesday night in the Athletics and Events Center, the Ithaca College chapter of Fellowship of Christian Athletes provides over 50 students with an opportunity to gather and share two intertwined passions: sports and their Christian faith. item.title: IT policy changes prompt community reaction
item.description: The Ithaca College Information Analytics and Technology team released an updated version of its IT policy Jan. 30, following multiple phishing attempts. The changes include new guidelines for the use of IC emails by faculty, staff and students, prompting mixed reactions from the community. item.title: Editorial: Black History Month is imperative to understanding all of history
item.description: Black History Month is imperative to understand the true history of the United States. While this month is not limited to the history of Black Americans, amidst the pushback against diversity, equity and inclusion policies, celebrating the achievements of Black Americans while equally acknowledging their unique experiences throughout our nation’s history is crucial.
